characters.name: Juan Carlos
characters.description: First-person narrator; sound artist and café worker in the Bronx, twenty-five years old; runs a building-listening practice he calls Chismosa; son of Mamá, grandson of the abuela; carries a warm coin in his pocket. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Rent was due in nine days.

characters.name: Mamá
characters.description: The narrator's mother; up before the power returns; cooks the tres golpes when she suspects the world is about to hit him; deflects questions about the past. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: She makes on days she suspects the world is about to hit me first.

characters.name: The narrator's grandmother
aliases: Mamá (as Mr. Rodríguez says 'Ask your mother' / 'Ask Mamá')
characters.description: Mentioned-only; old, stubborn, called the night before the blackout and asked whether 'it' had already started. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: She asked if it already started.

characters.name: Doña Fela
characters.description: Mentioned-only neighbor on the fifth floor who attributes the blackout to the Lord; also remembered on Mr. Rodríguez's map as 'Casa Fela, shoe repair, 1968–1994'. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Doña Fela on five says it was the Lord.

characters.name: Papá
characters.description: Mentioned-only; the narrator's father, absent on certain nights when the narrator was nine. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: I asked where Papá went on the nights he wasn’t home

characters.name: The super
characters.description: Mentioned-only building superintendent who blames Con Ed for the blackout. Physical appearance unspecified.

characters.name: Hi-vis construction worker
characters.description: Unnamed worker bolting the Aperture Civic banner to the scaffold; holds the ladder; headphones around his neck; union, daylight-only hours. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: The one holding the ladder had headphones around his neck.

characters.name: Mr. Rodríguez
characters.description: Owner of El Disco Café (formerly Discos Quisqueya) under the El on Jerome; a poet; keeps a hand-drawn map of the block's lost businesses; has his father's eyebrows. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: Mr. Rodríguez owns the café the way a cat owns a house.

characters.name: Manny
characters.description: The narrator's best friend since age nine; drummer, six-three, built like a refrigerator that learned to dance; plays in three bands; brings two iced coffees; calms the café's noise when he touches his drum case. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: He is six-three and built like a refrigerator that learned to dance

characters.name: Yari
characters.description: Friend who texts the narrator daily around ten, between her last patient and her first nap, checking whether he has eaten. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Yari texts me every day around ten, between her last patient and her first nap.

characters.name: Sofía
characters.description: Mentioned-only friend to whom the narrator forwards the Aperture Civic email preview; expected to make a spreadsheet with tabs. Physical appearance unspecified.

characters.name: Adrian Vale
characters.description: Mentioned-only signatory of the Aperture Civic email offering the narrator a commission for Founders' Night at the Kingsbridge Armory. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: — Adrian Vale, Director of Community Partnerships

characters.name: The kid from Soundview
characters.description: Mentioned-only young client whose beat-mixed EP the narrator finished but cannot bring himself to send. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: a kid in Soundview who wanted his EP to sound like it cost more than it did

characters.name: Rafa
characters.description: Mentioned-only; runs a percussion circle in the park on Sundays that Manny invites the narrator to. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: Rafa’s circle in the park, you coming?

characters.name: Man behind the register (Discos Quisqueya, 1973)
aliases: the man with a mustache and a good shirt
characters.description: ECHO vision figure; mustached shopkeeper in a good shirt behind the Discos Quisqueya register in August 1973; has Mr. Rodríguez's eyebrows half a century early; a mambo plays on his shelf radio. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: he had Mr. Rodríguez’s eyebrows, half a century early.

characters.name: Kid buying two copies of the same record
characters.description: ECHO vision figure; fifteen or sixteen, shell-toe Adidas, milk crate on his hip; buys two copies of the same record paid in quarters, grinning 'Todavía no' about turntables. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: Fifteen, maybe sixteen, shell-toe Adidas, a milk crate on his hip.

characters.name: Thin man in a brown suit
characters.description: ECHO vision figure; thin man in a brown suit with a small notebook at the dark end of the 1973 counter; writes quick, neat marks; looks up at the exact spot where the narrator stands fifty-three years later; holds his head like the man in headphones in the lit window. Physical appearance otherwise unspecified.
characters.evidence: A thin man in a brown suit, a small notebook.

characters.name: The freelancer
characters.description: Unnamed café patron at the corner table nursing one drip coffee for three hours; her keyboard is one of the café's six noises; stares after the narrator's vision. Physical appearance unspecified.
characters.evidence: the freelancer at the corner table who’d been nursing one drip coffee for three hours

characters.name: El Disco Café patrons (ensemble)
characters.description: Collective ensemble of the morning café crowd: two guys arguing about the Yankees' bullpen, a stroller baby who sighs and closes her eyes, a customer wanting oat milk in a cortado. Individual appearances unspecified.
characters.evidence: two guys arguing about the Yankees’ bullpen

scenes.name: Breakfast after the blackout
scenes.description: Morning kitchen scene: Mamá turns salami, the radio plays merengue low, the power went out at three and returned at four; she serves the tres golpes and reports the abuela's question about whether 'it' had started; the coin is warm in the narrator's pocket and something quiet for twenty-five years clears its throat.
scenes.evidence: La luz se fue a las tres y volvió a las cuatro

scenes.name: The Aperture Civic banner across the street
scenes.description: The narrator leaves for work and sees the empty building's new four-story vinyl banner — smiling people before a mural, 'A CALMER BLOCK STARTS HERE', and a camera-iris logo he recognizes and doesn't want to; a hi-vis worker confirms union daylight-only hours; the third-floor window stays dark.

scenes.name: El Disco Café: Mr. Rodríguez and the map of the block
scenes.description: The café under the El shakes with each train; Mr. Rodríguez teases the narrator's haunted face, lays out the three gigs and the rent math, then shows his two-year hand-drawn map of vanished Jerome Avenue businesses and hands the narrator a blank card to record the Ballroom's history.
scenes.evidence: So the block can check its own story.

scenes.name: Manny arrives with iced coffees
scenes.description: Manny shoulders through the door backward with a drum case and two iced coffees; when his palm rests on the case the café's six noises become one and the stroller baby sleeps; he needles the narrator about the unsent EP and invites him to Rafa's Sunday circle in the park.
scenes.evidence: The second Manny’s hand touched the case, those six noises quit being six and became one

scenes.name: Yari's daily text
scenes.description: Brief exchange: Yari texts 'did you eat', the narrator deflects with a photo of Manny's iced coffee, and she replies with a single skull.

scenes.name: The Aperture Civic email
scenes.description: At 10:40 an email from Adrian Vale of Aperture Civic arrives praising the narrator's 'building-listening practice' and offering a Founders' Night commission at the Kingsbridge Armory; the coin heats through the denim, the steamer's whistle sags flat; the narrator forwards it to Sofía, shows Manny, and refuses despite Manny's kind push; later he realizes nobody had ever called it 'building-listening' before.

scenes.name: ECHO: Discos Quisqueya, August 1973
scenes.description: ECHO vision triggered when the 4 train's scream and the steamer's whistle land on the same note: the café floor becomes the 1973 record shop, wooden bins of 45s, 'HOY NO FÍA, MAÑANA SÍ' over the register; the mustached man sells two copies of one record to a kid with a milk crate; at the dark end of the counter a thin man in a brown suit tallies the sale and looks up at the exact spot where the narrator stands.
scenes.evidence: HOY NO SE FÍA, MAÑANA SÍ.

scenes.name: Aftermath: the overflowing latte and the Ballroom card
scenes.description: Manny wakes the narrator from the vision; milk runs hot over his knuckles unnoticed; he performs steady through twenty cortados, works out what bothered him about the email's phrase 'building-listening', writes 'Ballroom, Saturday nights, mambo bands. Ask Mamá.' on a card and pins it to the empty corner of Jerome on the map.
scenes.evidence: Ballroom, Saturday nights, mambo bands. Ask Mamá.
